title: Streaming-to-batch embedding pipeline with job-level idempotency and adaptive backpressure
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: provide a single, resilient ingestion surface that accepts high-volume streaming writes and converts them into efficient backend batches for the embeddings service and downstream reranking. This ticket designs and implements a streaming-to-batch orchestration layer ("conveyor") that: accepts NDJSON/streamed records, validates and normalizes inputs, checkpoints progress, groups records into backend batches according to model/quantization/prefetch rules, and exposes an async job API for large imports. Core requirements: 1) Exactly-once delivery semantics for customer-provided records through idempotency keys + job checkpoints; 2) Low tail-latency for small streaming writes while maintaining cost-efficiency for bulk workloads through adaptive batching; 3) Robust automatic retries with exponential backoff and per-record error classification; 4) Observability: per-job token counts, per-shard latency percentiles, failed record rates, and rerank-quality drift signals. This implementation will reduce per-token overhead for bulk imports, provide a production-ready streaming path for real-time pipelines, and simplify deduplication needs for customers who previously had to manage idempotency themselves.
acceptance_criteria: API: New /v1/embeds/streaming-upsert endpoint accepts streaming NDJSON and returns a job_id for large uploads
Exactly-once semantics: client-provided idempotency_key + server checkpoints ensure duplicate records are not stored or scored more than once within a job scope
Hybrid latency: single-record streaming latencies under 150ms p50 for hosted tier; bulk batch throughput achieves >= 90% GPU utilization for large import jobs
Retries: transient infra errors trigger automatic retries with exponential backoff and bounded retries; permanent errors are surfaced per-record in job result manifest
Backpressure: service signals (HTTP 429 or streaming pause) when memory or batch queue depth exceeds configured thresholds
Observability: dashboards show job-level throughput, per-record error breakdown, idempotency collision rate, and rerank quality regression alerts
Migration: existing bulk NDJSON upload users can opt into new path without downtime; compatibility adapter available for older clients
design_decisions: Hybrid model: keep a low-latency fast-path for small/interactive streams and a background batching path for large jobs; switching is driven by job size heuristics and per-tenant signals

Idempotency granularity: idempotency_key scopes to (tenant, job_id, idempotency_key) with server-side monotonic checkpoints stored in the job ledger. Keys are 256-bit base64 to avoid collisions and truncated in logs for PII safety
Checkpointing: use append-only job ledger with per-shard offsets to enable resume after failure and to provide accurate progress metrics

Retry strategy: classify errors into transient (cpu/gpu infra, network), recoverable (model OOM -> smaller batch), and permanent (invalid input). Retries are automatic for transient and recoverable, with backoff and jitter
Partial failures: per-record failure manifests are stored in the job result S3/GCS manifest and linked from the job object; customers can request reprocessing of failed records
Security: payloads are encrypted at rest by default and idempotency keys never logged in full. Security review is required for ledger design and cross-tenant isolation
api_contract_proposal: Endpoints: 1) POST /v1/embeds/streaming-upsert (streaming NDJSON) -> returns job_id and optional immediate ack for first N records. Supports header: Idempotency-Key and Tenant-ID. 2) POST /v1/embeds/jobs (submit NDJSON file reference or manifest) -> creates async job. 3) GET /v1/embeds/jobs/{job_id} -> job status + manifest link. Job states: queued, ingesting, batching, applying, completed, failed, cancelled. Job manifest: total_records, successful_records, failed_records, storage_manifest_url. Streaming protocol: SSE-compatible progress updates over an optional websocket for subscribed clients.
operational_plan: Phase 1 (PoC): implement conveyor prototype in staging that accepts streaming NDJSON, checkpoints to a local ledger, and emits fixed-size batches to the embeddings runner
Phase 2 (Canary): route 5% of small interactive traffic and 100% of new bulk jobs for a subset of tenants behind feature flag; collect latency, error, and duplication metrics
Phase 3 (Rollout): enforce idempotency semantics, enable auto-retries, and turn on adaptive batching defaults for all new customers. Provide opt-in migration path for existing customers
Phase 4 (GA): expose advanced knobs in Console (batch_size_target, max_inflight_batches, retry_policy), add RBAC controls for job manifests, and document SLAs
test_plan: Unit: ledger checkpointing, idempotency key collisions, batch serialization correctness
Integration: end-to-end streaming upsert -> job completion against staging embeddings runner (small and large models)
Chaos: simulate pod restarts, transient GPU OOM, and network partitions to validate resume semantics
Performance: throughput benchmarks for small-interactive vs bulk imports; measure GPU utilization and per-token cost
Security: threat model review for idempotency key storage and manifest access; penetration test on job manifest URLs
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: idempotency collisions could drop legitimate writes if keys reused maliciously. Mitigation: require authenticated tenant-scoped keys and TTL-based key expiry; surface suspicious collision alerts
Risk: backpressure misconfiguration may cause cascade 429s. Mitigation: conservative defaults, circuit breaker per-tenant, and queue-length autosizing
Risk: large job manifests leak PII. Mitigation: redact payloads from manifests, store only hashes, and encrypt manifests with tenant KMS
rollout_notes: Canary group: platform-test-tenants, internal sandbox orgs, and 3 low-latency pilot customers
Migration doc: write a migration guide with code snippets for SDKs (Python/Go/Node) showing streaming + idempotency usage
